summary: Deploy conditional Slack bridge for cross-pod thread escalations with Confluence snapshot and audit trail
description:
Issue summary: We need a conditional Slack->Confluence bridge that automatically escalates long-running or unresolved cross-pod threads into a lightweight Confluence snapshot and creates an internal Jira ticket for audit and follow-up.

Why: Cross-pod incident and coordination threads often become noisy and lose context when they hit operational limits (e.g., >3 days open, >50 messages, or require oncall intervention). Engineering and SRE teams ask for a low-friction escalation path that preserves thread context, attachments, and selected messages for asynchronous review and compliance.

Impact: Reduces context-loss during handoffs, provides an auditable record for post-incident review, and reduces repeated manual copy/paste and screenshotting. Initial rollout targets runtime-ops and infra-pod channels.

Proposed design: 1) A Slack bot listens for configured triggers (thread age, message count, explicit /escalate command, mention of @ops-escalate). 2) On trigger, bot builds a Confluence page draft containing thread title, top N messages, attachments (links), and a short summary drafted using a templated prompt. 3) A Jira ticket (INT- prefixed) is created in the internal-support project with the Confluence link, and the originating thread receives a notification linking the ticket. 4) RBAC: only members of a configured escalation group can approve automatic publication; otherwise the draft is created in a sandbox namespace and emailed to the approvers. 5) All actions are logged to an audit channel and stored with an immutable timestamp.

Rollout plan: Stage1: deploy to staging with runtime-ops and infra-pod channels; manual approval required. Stage2: enable automatic draft generation but require human publish. Stage3: conditional auto-publish for channels on the safe-list and for threads tagged with #escalate-auto.

Acceptance criteria: - Bot creates a Confluence draft with message history and metadata for all triggers in staging. - Created Jira tickets include Confluence link and preserve thread context. - Access controls prevent auto-publication unless channel is in safe-list. - Audit log entries are emitted for every action.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-02: Reviewed existing slack-bot infra; current bot framework supports slash commands and outgoing webhooks but lacks Confluence writer integration.
2026-03-03: Validated Confluence REST API auth flows using service account 'automation-bot@redwood.com' and confirmed page creation with macro templates works in a sandbox space.
2026-03-04: Confirmed Jira automation API can create issues in internal-support with link to Confluence page; need to ensure issue naming uses INT- prefix avoidance collision rules.
2026-03-05: RBAC model: propose using existing SSO groups (team:runtime-ops, team:infra) mapped to a new 'escalation-approvers' group in Confluence/Jira for publish rights.
2026-03-09: Performance check: exporting thread of 500 messages to Confluence draft takes ~2.1s in staging; need rate-limit backoffs if attachments >10.
comments: 2026-03-02 - Aisha Patel: Filing request after a runtime-ops postmortem where context was lost over a weekend. Requesting lightweight, auditable handoff flow.
2026-03-04 - SRE Lead (Morgan Lee): We should ensure this respects retention policy and PII redaction — any snapshot must run a sanitization pass before publishing.
2026-03-06 - Marco Diaz: Prototype Confluence draft generator working in sandbox; posting to this ticket with PR when ready. Leaving auto-publish disabled by default.
2026-03-10 - Security (Rina Okafor): Approving design contingent on adding a message-scrubber step and explicit config for which channels are allowed to auto-publish.
2026-03-12 - Product Ops (Evan Brooks): Please add a small UX flow for the requester to annotate the draft summary before final publish. Important for cross-team clarity.
resolution: In Progress: Prototype generator deployed to staging and creating drafts. Pending: implement PII scrubber, safe-list UI, and on-approve publish workflow. Next steps: secure approval from Security and Product Ops, then run a 2-week staged pilot in runtime-ops channels.
